claim: β-catenin regulates self-renewal and differentiation of mammalian nephron progenitor cells (NPCs).
source: The canonical Wnt pathway transcriptional co-activator β-catenin regulates self-renewal and differentiation of mammalian nephron progenitor cells (NPCs).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise of the study.

claim: Low CHIR-mediated maintenance and expansion of NPCs are independent of direct engagement of TCF/LEF/β-catenin transcriptional complexes at low CHIR-dependent cell-cycle targets.
source: Low CHIR-mediated maintenance and expansion of NPCs are independent of direct engagement of TCF/LEF/β-catenin transcriptional complexes at low CHIR-dependent cell-cycle targets.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data analysis in the manuscript.

claim: In high CHIR, TCF7/LEF1/β-catenin complexes replaced TCF7L1/TCF7L2 binding on enhancers of differentiation-promoting target genes.
source: In contrast, in high CHIR, TCF7/LEF1/β-catenin complexes replaced TCF7L1/TCF7L2 binding on enhancers of differentiation-promoting target genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through ChIP-seq analysis comparing low and high CHIR conditions.

claim: Chromosome conformation studies showed pre-established promoter–enhancer connections to target genes in NPCs.
source: Chromosome confirmation studies showed pre-established promoter–enhancer connections to these target genes in NPCs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Hi-C data presented in the manuscript.

claim: High CHIR-associated de novo looping was observed in positive transcriptional feedback regulation to the canonical Wnt pathway.
source: High CHIR-associated de novo looping was observed in positive transcriptional feedback regulation to the canonical Wnt pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through Hi-C analysis showing new chromatin loops in high CHIR conditions.

claim: β-catenin's direct transcriptional role is restricted to the induction of NPCs.
source: Thus, β-catenin's direct transcriptional role is restricted to the induction of NPCs, where rising β-catenin levels switch inhibitory TCF7L1/TCF7L2 complexes to activating LEF1/TCF7 complexes at primed gene targets poised for rapid initiation of a nephrogenic program.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the collective findings of the study.

claim: Rising β-catenin levels switch inhibitory TCF7L1/TCF7L2 complexes to activating LEF1/TCF7 complexes at primed gene targets.
source: Thus, β-catenin's direct transcriptional role is restricted to the induction of NPCs, where rising β-catenin levels switch inhibitory TCF7L1/TCF7L2 complexes to activating LEF1/TCF7 complexes at primed gene targets poised for rapid initiation of a nephrogenic program.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing differential TCF/LEF binding.

claim: In the absence of Wnt ligand, Tcf transcription factors bind enhancers of Wnt target genes recruiting co-repressors to silence target gene expression.
source: In the absence of Wnt ligand, HMG box family Tcf transcription factors bind enhancers of Wnt target genes recruiting co-repressors (Tle, Ctbp, and others) to silence target gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as part of the classical model of canonical Wnt signaling in the introduction.

claim: In the cytoplasm, β-catenin is phosphorylated by an axin/GSK3β-dependent β-catenin destruction complex, resulting in ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation.
source: In the cytoplasm, the transcriptional co-activator β-catenin is phosphorylated by an axin/GSK3β-dependent β-catenin destruction complex, resulting in ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is stated as part of the classical model of canonical Wnt signaling in the introduction.

claim: Upon Wnt ligand binding to Fzd receptor/Lrp co-receptors, the β-catenin destruction complex is sequestered to the activated receptor protein complex through axin interactions.
source: Upon Wnt ligand binding to Fzd receptor/Lrp co-receptors on the cell surface, the β-catenin destruction complex is sequestered to the activated receptor protein complex through axin interactions, removing β-catenin from GSK3β-directed, phosphorylation-mediated degradation (Schaefer and Peifer, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as part of the classical model of canonical Wnt signaling in the introduction with citation support.

claim: As a result of increasing β-catenin levels, β-catenin is free to associate with TCF/LEF DNA binding partners, activating Wnt target gene transcription.
source: As a result of increasing β-catenin levels, β-catenin is free to associate with TCF/LEF DNA binding partners, activating Wnt target gene transcription (Mosimann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as part of the classical model of canonical Wnt signaling in the introduction with citation support.

claim: All four mammalian Tcf family members are able to functionally interact with both Tle family co-repressors and β-catenin.
source: While evidence suggests that all four mammalian Tcf family members are able to functionally interact with both Tle family co-repressors and β-catenin (Brantjes et al., 2001), a variety of studies in a range of biological systems indicate that Tcf7l1 predominantly acts as a repressor, Tcf7l2 as a context-dependent activator or repressor, and Tcf7 and Lef1 as transcriptional activators, of Wnt target gene expression (Lien and Fuchs, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support from Brantjes et al., 2001.

claim: Tcf7l1 predominantly acts as a repressor of Wnt target gene expression.
source: While evidence suggests that all four mammalian Tcf family members are able to functionally interact with both Tle family co-repressors and β-catenin (Brantjes et al., 2001), a variety of studies in a range of biological systems indicate that Tcf7l1 predominantly acts as a repressor, Tcf7l2 as a context-dependent activator or repressor, and Tcf7 and Lef1 as transcriptional activators, of Wnt target gene expression (Lien and Fuchs, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support from Lien and Fuchs, 2014.

claim: Tcf7l2 acts as a context-dependent activator or repressor of Wnt target gene expression.
source: While evidence suggests that all four mammalian Tcf family members are able to functionally interact with both Tle family co-repressors and β-catenin (Brantjes et al., 2001), a variety of studies in a range of biological systems indicate that Tcf7l1 predominantly acts as a repressor, Tcf7l2 as a context-dependent activator or repressor, and Tcf7 and Lef1 as transcriptional activators, of Wnt target gene expression (Lien and Fuchs, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support from Lien and Fuchs, 2014.

claim: Tcf7 and Lef1 act as transcriptional activators of Wnt target gene expression.
source: While evidence suggests that all four mammalian Tcf family members are able to functionally interact with both Tle family co-repressors and β-catenin (Brantjes et al., 2001), a variety of studies in a range of biological systems indicate that Tcf7l1 predominantly acts as a repressor, Tcf7l2 as a context-dependent activator or repressor, and Tcf7 and Lef1 as transcriptional activators, of Wnt target gene expression (Lien and Fuchs, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support from Lien and Fuchs, 2014.

claim: The adult mammalian kidney arises from distinct cell populations within the intermediate mesoderm.
source: The adult (metanephric) mammalian kidney arises from distinct cell populations within the intermediate mesoderm (McMahon, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: All nephrons arise from a small pool of a few hundred nephron progenitor cells established at the onset of kidney development.
source: All nephrons – the repeating functional unit of the kidney – arise from a small pool of a few hundred nephron progenitor cells (NPCs) established at the onset of kidney development (Short et al., 2014; Kobayashi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The mouse kidney contains approximately 14,000 nephrons.
source: The subsequent balance in the maintenance, expansion, and commitment of NPCs is critical to ensuring a full complement of nephrons, approximately 14,000 in the mouse and 1 million in the human kidney (Bertram et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The human kidney contains approximately 1 million nephrons.
source: The subsequent balance in the maintenance, expansion, and commitment of NPCs is critical to ensuring a full complement of nephrons, approximately 14,000 in the mouse and 1 million in the human kidney (Bertram et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: A reduced nephron endowment has been associated with abnormal kidney function and disease susceptibility.
source: A reduced nephron endowment has been associated with abnormal kidney function and disease susceptibility (Luyckx and Brenner, 2010; McMahon, 2016; Bertram et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The maintenance and expansion of NPCs are supported by Fgf, Bmp, and Wnt signals produced by NPCs or adjacent mesenchymal interstitial progenitor and ureteric epithelial cell types.
source: The maintenance and expansion of NPCs are supported by Fgf, Bmp, and Wnt signals produced by NPCs or adjacent mesenchymal interstitial progenitor and ureteric epithelial cell types (McMahon, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Ureteric epithelium-derived Wnt9b acts on NPCs in a β-catenin-dependent transcriptional process to regulate NPC target gene expression and expansion of the nephron progenitor pool.
source: Within this nephrogenic niche, ureteric epithelium-derived Wnt9b is thought to act on NPCs in a β-catenin-dependent transcriptional process to regulate NPC target gene expression and expansion of the nephron progenitor pool (Karner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Removal of Wnt9b from the ureteric epithelium and NPC-specific production of β-catenin results in the failure of NPC differentiation.
source: The removal of Wnt9b from the ureteric epithelium and NPC-specific production of β-catenin also results in the failure of NPC differentiation (Carroll et al., 2005), whereas chemical inhibition of GSK3β (Davies and Garrod, 1995; Kuure et al., 2007), or genetic activation within NPCs of a β-catenin form insensitive to GSK phosphorylation-mediated proteasomal degradation, leads to Wnt9b-independent ectopic induction of differentiation-promoting gene targets (Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Chemical inhibition of GSK3β leads to Wnt9b-independent ectopic induction of differentiation-promoting gene targets.
source: The removal of Wnt9b from the ureteric epithelium and NPC-specific production of β-catenin also results in the failure of NPC differentiation (Carroll et al., 2005), whereas chemical inhibition of GSK3β (Davies and Garrod, 1995; Kuure et al., 2007), or genetic activation within NPCs of a β-catenin form insensitive to GSK phosphorylation-mediated proteasomal degradation, leads to Wnt9b-independent ectopic induction of differentiation-promoting gene targets (Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Genetic activation within NPCs of a β-catenin form insensitive to GSK phosphorylation-mediated proteasomal degradation leads to Wnt9b-independent ectopic induction of differentiation-promoting gene targets.
source: The removal of Wnt9b from the ureteric epithelium and NPC-specific production of β-catenin also results in the failure of NPC differentiation (Carroll et al., 2005), whereas chemical inhibition of GSK3β (Davies and Garrod, 1995; Kuure et al., 2007), or genetic activation within NPCs of a β-catenin form insensitive to GSK phosphorylation-mediated proteasomal degradation, leads to Wnt9b-independent ectopic induction of differentiation-promoting gene targets (Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Different levels of β-catenin distinguish maintenance and commitment of NPCs.
source: Genetic and chemical modification of Wnt pathway components suggest different levels of β-catenin distinguish maintenance and commitment of NPCs (Ramalingam et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: β-catenin engages at TCF/LEF recognition motifs within enhancers linked to genes driving NPC differentiation.
source: Genomic analysis of β-catenin engagement at TCF/LEF recognition motifs within enhancers linked to genes driving NPC differentiation (Park et al., 2012), and subsequent transgenic studies demonstrating TCF/LEF-dependent activity of cis regulatory elements, provides strong evidence for a canonical Wnt/β-catenin/Tcf regulatory axis (Mosimann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling directs opposing NPC programs: maintenance and expansion of uncommitted NPCs and their commitment to nephron formation.
source: Thus, canonical Wnt signaling directs opposing NPC programs: maintenance and expansion of uncommitted NPCs and their commitment to nephron formation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a summary of the biological context.

claim: A low level of CHIR (1.25 µM) is an essential component in NPEM medium supporting the expansion of NPCs while maintaining the nephron-forming competence.
source: A low level of CHIR (1.25 µM) is an essential component in NPEM medium supporting the expansion of NPCs while maintaining the nephron-forming competence (Brown et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Within 3 days of elevating CHIR levels (3 µM), aggregate NPC cultures show a robust signature of nephron differentiation.
source: Within 3 days of elevating CHIR levels (3 µM), aggregate NPC cultures show a robust signature of nephron differentiation (Brown et al., 2015; Ramalingam et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Low CHIR conditions maintained Six2 but did not induce expression of Jag1.
source: As expected, low CHIR conditions maintained Six2, a key determinant of the NPC state, but did not induce expression of Jag1 (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), a Notch pathway ligand activity at early stage of mouse and human NPC commitment (Georgas et al., 2009; Lindström et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: A significant increase of cellular and nuclear β-catenin was observed in 5 µM CHIR.
source: A significant increase of cellular and nuclear β-catenin (Figure 1A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) was observed in 5 µM CHIR ('high CHIR' throughout), along with a strong inductive response: Six2 protein level persisted, but there was a robust induction of Jag1 (Figure 1A–C), mirroring early inductive events in the pre-tubular aggregate and renal vesicle in vivo (Lindström et al., 2018b; Mugford et al., 2009; Georgas et al., 2009; Xu et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In 5 µM CHIR, Six2 protein level persisted and there was a robust induction of Jag1.
source: A significant increase of cellular and nuclear β-catenin (Figure 1A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) was observed in 5 µM CHIR ('high CHIR' throughout), along with a strong inductive response: Six2 protein level persisted, but there was a robust induction of Jag1 (Figure 1A–C), mirroring early inductive events in the pre-tubular aggregate and renal vesicle in vivo (Lindström et al., 2018b; Mugford et al., 2009; Georgas et al., 2009; Xu et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Low CHIR maintains expression of transcriptional regulators required for NPC specification and/or maintenance, including Pax2, Wt1, Hoxa/d11, and Sall1.
source: Low CHIR maintains expression of transcriptional regulators required for NPC specification and/or maintenance, including Pax2, Wt1, Hoxa/d11, and Sall1 (Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1; McMahon, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: High CHIR led to a downregulation of regulators and markers of self-renewing NPCs, including Six2, Cited1, Osr1, and Eya1.
source: In contrast, high CHIR led to a downregulation of regulators and markers of self-renewing NPCs, including Six2 (Self et al., 2006), Cited1 (Mugford et al., 2009), Osr1 (Xu et al., 2014a), and Eya1 (Xu et al., 2014b), and a concomitant increase in expression of genes associated with induction of nephrogenesis, such as Wnt4, Jag1, Lhx1, and Fgf8 (Figure 1C; Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: High CHIR led to a concomitant increase in expression of genes associated with induction of nephrogenesis, such as Wnt4, Jag1, Lhx1, and Fgf8.
source: In contrast, high CHIR led to a downregulation of regulators and markers of self-renewing NPCs, including Six2 (Self et al., 2006), Cited1 (Mugford et al., 2009), Osr1 (Xu et al., 2014a), and Eya1 (Xu et al., 2014b), and a concomitant increase in expression of genes associated with induction of nephrogenesis, such as Wnt4, Jag1, Lhx1, and Fgf8 (Figure 1C; Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: More than 90% of isolated cells were Six2+.
source: Comparing input NPCs freshly isolated from the kidney cortex with NPC-free cortical preparations (NFC), the strong enrichment for NPC-relevant GO terms (Figure 1D, top panel) was consistent with a strong enrichment of Six2+ NPCs (more than 90% of isolated cells were Six2+).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the purity of NPC isolation.

claim: When NPCs cultured in high versus low CHIR conditions were compared, a strong enrichment was observed in terms associated with Wnt signaling pathway.
source: When NPCs cultured in high versus low CHIR conditions were compared, a strong enrichment was observed in terms associated with Wnt signaling pathway, as expected, on CHIR-mediated NPC induction (Figure 1D, middle and bottom panels).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Primary NPCs and their counterpart in low CHIR showed similar expression patterns for NPC self-renewal and differentiation markers.
source: Although primary NPCs, and their counterpart in low CHIR, showed similar expression patterns for NPC self-renewal and differentiation markers, transcriptome-wide comparison of all samples clustered primary NPCs into a distinct group from NPCs cultured in either low or high CHIR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Transcriptome-wide comparison of all samples clustered primary NPCs into a distinct group from NPCs cultured in either low or high CHIR.
source: Although primary NPCs, and their counterpart in low CHIR, showed similar expression patterns for NPC self-renewal and differentiation markers, transcriptome-wide comparison of all samples clustered primary NPCs into a distinct group from NPCs cultured in either low or high CHIR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The distinct clustering of primary NPCs is explained by a pronounced metabolic shift in culture with strong enrichment in metabolic processes such as sterol biosynthesis.
source: This is explained by a pronounced metabolic shift in culture where there is a strong enrichment in GO analysis in metabolic processes such as sterol biosynthesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Freshly isolated NPCs showed a low-level inductive signature reflecting a co-contribution of small numbers of early induced NPCs.
source: In addition, freshly isolated NPCs showed a low-level inductive signature reflecting a co-contribution of small numbers of early induced NPCs (expression of Fgf8, Wnt4, Lhx1, Heyl, Bmp4, Mafb, and Podxl, Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Within 24 hr, low CHIR culture stabilized an undifferentiated NPCs signature with the downregulation of induction markers.
source: Within 24 hr, low CHIR culture stabilized an undifferentiated NPCs signature with the downregulation of induction markers (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: NPEM culture establishes a more rigorous model for distinguishing uninduced versus induced NPC responses than is possible with the intrinsic heterogeneity within primary isolates of NPC populations.
source: Importantly, these data show that NPEM culture establishes a more rigorous model for distinguishing uninduced versus induced NPC responses than is possible with the intrinsic heterogeneity within primary isolates of NPC populations.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comparison of primary and cultured NPCs.

claim: In low CHIR conditions, the Six2DE shows an open and active configuration: an ATAC-seq peak, flanked by H3K27ac peaks with Pol II engagement at the enhancer and within the gene body.
source: In low CHIR conditions, the Six2DE shows an open and active configuration: an ATAC-seq peak, flanked by H3K27ac peaks with Pol II engagement at the enhancer and within the gene body.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing chromatin features at the Six2 distal enhancer.

claim: In high CHIR, ATAC-seq, H3K27ac, and Pol II ChIP-Seq signals at the Six2DE were reduced, correlating with the downregulation of gene expression.
source: In high CHIR, ATAC-seq, H3K27ac, and Pol II ChIP-Seq signals were reduced, correlating with the downregulation of gene expression (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The Wnt4DE displayed an opposite trend in the shift from low to high CHIR: the ATAC and H3K27ac ChIP signals increased together with increased Pol II engagement in the gene body.
source: As predicted, the Wnt4DE displayed an opposite trend in the shift from low to high CHIR: the ATAC and H3K27ac ChIP signals increased together with increased Pol II engagement in the gene body.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing chromatin features at the Wnt4 distal enhancer.

claim: A marked enhancer-specific Pol II ChIP-seq signature was visible in low CHIR NPC maintenance conditions and reduced on initiation of active transcription in high CHIR.
source: Surprisingly, a marked enhancer-specific Pol II ChIP-seq signature was visible in low CHIR NPC maintenance conditions and reduced on initiation of active transcription in high CHIR (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: NPC-specific DARs were significantly enriched in transcription factor binding sites for Six, Pax, and Hox factors.
source: NPC-specific DARs were significantly enriched in transcription factor binding sites for Six, Pax, and Hox factors consistent with the critical roles of Six1/2, Pax2, and Hox11 paralogues in NPC programs (Figure 2C; Naiman et al., 2017; Self et al., 2006; Wellik et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: GO-GREAT analysis predicted that NPC-specific DARs were enriched near genes linked to kidney development.
source: Functionally, GO-GREAT analysis (McLean et al., 2010) predicted that these regions were enriched near genes linked to kidney development (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Most of the DARs are distal to the transcriptional start site (TSS) of genes, indicative of enhancer elements.
source: Most of the DARs are distal to the transcriptional start site (TSS) of genes, indicative of enhancer elements (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by distance distribution shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The top two motifs identified in high CHIR-specific DARs were the Jun (AP-1) and TCF/LEF motifs.
source: The top two motifs identified in high CHIR-specific DARs were the Jun (AP-1) and TCF/LEF motifs (Figure 2C), supporting a β-catenin-driven increase in accessibility through engagement with TCF/LEF factors.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Phosphorylated Jun has been detected in both NPCs and differentiates renal vesicles.
source: Phosphorylated Jun has been detected in both NPCs and differentiates renal vesicles (Muthukrishnan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Jun binds Tcf7l2 to cooperatively activate gene expression in Wnt-dependent intestinal tumors.
source: Further, Jun binds Tcf7l2 to cooperatively activate gene expression in Wnt-dependent intestinal tumors (Nateri et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Elevated expression of Jun, Junb, and Jund in high CHIR suggests a potential interplay of Jun family members with β-catenin/Tcf-driven NPC differentiation.
source: Elevated expression of Jun, Junb, and Jund in high CHIR (Supplementary file 1) suggests a potential interplay of Jun family members with β-catenin/Tcf-driven NPC differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The Wnt4DE was significantly more accessible in high CHIR versus low CHIR conditions.
source: Statistical assessment (Supplementary file 2) determined that the Wnt4DE was significantly more accessible in high CHIR versus low CHIR conditions (peak ID 16567, adjusted p-value=0.02).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical support from Supplementary file 2.

claim: The Six2DE showed a trend of greater accessibility in low CHIR versus high CHIR condition.
source: The Six2DE showed a trend of greater accessibility in low CHIR versus high CHIR condition (peak ID 10164, adjusted p-value=0.13).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical support.

claim: Differences in ATAC-Seq data are consistent with comparing FACS-purified E16 and P2 Six2GFP+ cells, where P2 NPCs are thought to have enhanced differentiation capability.
source: These observations are consistent with differences in ATAC-Seq data comparing FACS-purified E16 and P2 Six2GFP+ cells, where P2 NPCs are thought to have enhanced differentiation capability (Hilliard et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Tcf7l1, Tcf7l2, and Tcf7 transcripts were expressed at low (2–10 TPM; Tcf7l2 and Tcf7) or moderate (50 TPM; Tcf7l1) levels in low CHIR NPC maintenance conditions.
source: Of the four genes, Tcf7l1, Tcf7l2, and Tcf7 transcripts were expressed at low (2–10 TPM; Tcf7l2 and Tcf7) or moderate (50 TPM; Tcf7l1) levels in low CHIR NPC maintenance conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing RNA-seq expression levels.

claim: CHIR-mediated induction of NPCs resulted in a significant downregulation of Tcf7l1 expression.
source: CHIR-mediated induction of NPCs resulted in a significant downregulation of Tcf7l1 expression, while expression of both Tcf7 and Lef1 was markedly upregulated (Figure 3A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B').
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression of both Tcf7 and Lef1 was markedly upregulated in high CHIR.
source: CHIR-mediated induction of NPCs resulted in a significant downregulation of Tcf7l1 expression, while expression of both Tcf7 and Lef1 was markedly upregulated (Figure 3A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B').
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The same general trend in TCF/LEF expression was observed examining the level of each protein in the nucleus of NPCs through quantitative immunofluorescence and western blot analyses.
source: The same general trend was observed examining the level of each protein in the nucleus of NPCs through quantitative immunofluorescence (Figure 3B, C) and western blot (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence and western blot data.

claim: There is a significant decrease in Tcf7l2 protein but not transcript level in high CHIR versus low CHIR condition, suggesting transcriptionally independent regulation of Tcf7l2 activity.
source: Interestingly, there is a significant decrease in Tcf7l2 protein but not transcript level in high CHIR versus low CHIR condition, suggesting transcriptionally independent regulation of Tcf7l2 activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison of RNA-seq and protein data.

claim: In agreement with in vitro data, Tcf7l1 transcripts were enriched in self-renewing NPCs while Lef1 levels were elevated in differentiated NPCs in vivo.
source: In agreement with in vitro data, Tcf7l1 transcripts were enriched in self-renewing NPCs while Lef1 levels were elevated in differentiated NPCs, though Tcf7 and Tcf7l2 expression levels were relatively low, with little variation between non- and early induced NPC states (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by single-cell RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F.

claim: Tcf7 and Tcf7l2 expression levels were relatively low in vivo, with little variation between non- and early induced NPC states.
source: In agreement with in vitro data, Tcf7l1 transcripts were enriched in self-renewing NPCs while Lef1 levels were elevated in differentiated NPCs, though Tcf7 and Tcf7l2 expression levels were relatively low, with little variation between non- and early induced NPC states (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by single-cell RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C–F.

claim: Motif discovery of TCF/LEF/β-catenin ChIP-seq binding sites shows highest DNA motif enrichment as the TCF/LEF binding element, indicating a high specificity of the data sets.
source: Motif discovery of TCF/LEF/β-catenin ChIP-seq binding sites shows highest DNA motif enrichment as the TCF/LEF binding element, indicating a high specificity of the data sets and supporting direct TCF/LEF/β-catenin target interactions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A Hox motif is highly enriched in TCF/LEF binding sites in both low CHIR and high CHIR conditions consistent with Hox11 paralog regulation of the NPC state.
source: In addition, a Hox motif is highly enriched in TCF/LEF binding sites in both low CHIR and high CHIR conditions consistent with Hox11 paralog regulation of the NPC state (Wellik et al., 2002; Park et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: A Runx motif is enriched in TCF/LEF binding sites in high CHIR.
source: A Runx motif is enriched in TCF/LEF binding sites in high CHIR. Runx1 expression is upregulated in the same condition (Supplementary file 1), but the significance of possible Runx-dependent regulation remains to be determined.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by motif analysis and RNA-seq data.

claim: Tcf7l1 engagement at DNA targets was reduced on NPC induction.
source: Consistent with the different levels of each protein in low and high CHIR conditions, Tcf7l1 engagement at DNA targets was reduced on NPC induction, while Tcf7, Lef1, and β-catenin showed a marked increase in DNA bound sites (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Tcf7, Lef1, and β-catenin showed a marked increase in DNA bound sites on NPC induction.
source: Consistent with the different levels of each protein in low and high CHIR conditions, Tcf7l1 engagement at DNA targets was reduced on NPC induction, while Tcf7, Lef1, and β-catenin showed a marked increase in DNA bound sites (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In both low and high CHIR conditions, β-catenin association overlapped extensively with the binding of cognate TCF/LEF factors specifically enriched in each condition.
source: In both low and high CHIR conditions, β-catenin association overlapped extensively with the binding of cognate TCF/LEF factors specifically enriched in each condition (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Motif recovery suggests direct engagement of β-catenin through TCF/LEF binding sites in either CHIR condition.
source: In either CHIR condition, motif recovery suggests direct engagement through TCF/LEF binding sites (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Localization of β-catenin is primarily dependent on TCF/LEF factors, consistent with previous findings in murine intestinal studies.
source: This is consistent with previous findings in murine intestinal studies that localization of β-catenin is primarily dependent on TCF/LEF factors (Schuijers et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation support.

claim: Hierarchical clustering indicates that the general feature of TCF/LEF factor binding in low CHIR and high CHIR was distinct and determined by the condition.
source: Notably, hierarchical clustering indicates that the general feature of TCF/LEF factor binding in low CHIR and high CHIR was distinct and determined by the condition as different TCF/LEF factors targeted common genomic regions that differ between low CHIR and high CHIR conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Tcf7l2 mRNA and protein levels did not vary greatly between low and high CHIR conditions but Tcf7l2 DNA interactions differed significantly.
source: This observation was most evident examining Tcf7l2. Tcf7l2 mRNA and protein levels did not vary greatly between low and high CHIR conditions but Tcf7l2 DNA interactions differed significantly (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The switch in TCF/LEF factor binding at the Wnt4DE correlated with activation of Wnt4 expression.
source: This switch in TCF/LEF factor binding correlated with activation of Wnt4 expression, consistent with a potential repressive role for Tcf7l1/Tcf7l2 interactions and activating role for Tcf7/Lef1 engagement (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: β-catenin was engaged at the Wnt4DE in low CHIR condition where Wnt4 was transcriptionally silent.
source: Interestingly, β-catenin was engaged at the Wnt4DE in low CHIR condition where Wnt4 was transcriptionally silent, though β-catenin binding at this enhancer was increased on high CHIR induction of NPCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: β-catenin binding at the Wnt4DE was increased on high CHIR induction of NPCs.
source: Interestingly, β-catenin was engaged at the Wnt4DE in low CHIR condition where Wnt4 was transcriptionally silent, though β-catenin binding at this enhancer was increased on high CHIR induction of NPCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A marked switch in the binding signature of TCF/LEF factors is a more striking correlation with subsequent activation of Wnt4 transcription than the increase in β-catenin binding.
source: In summary, though elevating β-catenin levels through high CHIR stabilization of GSK3β lead to some increase in binding of β-catenin at the Wnt4 enhancer, a marked switch in the binding signature of TCF/LEF factors is a more striking correlation with subsequent activation of Wnt4 transcription.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: Comparing DNA regions bound by Tcf7l1 in low CHIR and those bound by Lef1 in high CHIR, a significant overlap was observed (p-value = 1e-569).
source: Comparing DNA regions bound by Tcf7l1 in low CHIR and those bound by Lef1 in high CHIR, we observed a significant overlap (p-value = 1e-569), though over half were unique to a data set (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Over half of the DNA regions bound by Tcf7l1 in low CHIR or Lef1 in high CHIR were unique to a data set.
source: Comparing DNA regions bound by Tcf7l1 in low CHIR and those bound by Lef1 in high CHIR, we observed a significant overlap (p-value = 1e-569), though over half were unique to a data set (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Only sets 2 and 3 TCF/LEF binding sites showed a strong prediction for direct TCF/LEF binding based on motif recovery.
source: Interestingly, examining motif recovery across sets 1–3 indicated that only sets 2 and 3 showed a strong prediction for direct TCF/LEF binding (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Tcf7l1 likely associates with a large number of DNA regions without direct DNA binding at TCF/LEF response elements.
source: Thus, Tcf7l1 likely associates with a large number of DNA regions without direct DNA binding at TCF/LEF response elements.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on motif analysis.

claim: 73% of Tcf7l1 sites bound in low CHIR with a predicted TCF/LEF motif overlapped with those bound by Lef1 in high CHIR.
source: The majority (73%) of Tcf7l1 sites bound in low CHIR with a predicted TCF/LEF motif overlapped with those bound by Lef1 in high CHIR (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Only 29% of Tcf7l1 binding sites without a TCF/LEF motif overlapped with Lef1 bound regions.
source: In contrast, only 29% of Tcfl71 binding sites without a TCF/LEF motif prediction overlapped with Lef1 bound regions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Switching from a Tcf7l1 to a Lef1-centered DNA interaction at TCF/LEF response elements was a general feature of NPC induction response.
source: Thus, switching from a Tcf7l1 to a Lef1-centered DNA interaction at TCF/LEF response elements was a general feature of NPC induction response.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on overlap analysis.

claim: Set 2 (switch) sites displayed stronger binding of Tcf7l2, Tcf7, Lef1, and β-catenin, as well as higher level of markers of activated chromatin in high CHIR condition compared to set 3 (de novo).
source: Comparing with set 3 (de novo), set 2 (switch) sites displayed stronger binding of Tcf7l2, Tcf7, Lef1, and β-catenin, as well as higher level of markers of activated chromatin (ATAC-Seq and H3K27ac ChIP-Seq) in high CHIR condition (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: TCF/LEF sites occupied by Tcf7l1 in low CHIR are poised for stronger binding by TCF/LEF activators in high CHIR condition.
source: Thus, the data suggests that TCF/LEF sites occupied by Tcf7l1 in low CHIR are poised for stronger binding (and therefore activation) by TCF/LEF activators in high CHIR condition.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: GO GREAT analysis of all three sets of TCF/LEF binding sites predicted expected kidney terms such as 'metanephric nephron morphogenesis' or 'renal vesicle morphogenesis'.
source: Interestingly, GO GREAT analysis of all three sets predicted expected kidney terms such as 'metanephric nephron morphogenesis' or 'renal vesicle morphogenesis' (Figure 4E), consistent with biologically relevant interactions, arguing against artifactual responses to culture or CHIR treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: More than half (60%) of the potential target genes of set 2 'switch' sites overlap with those of set 3 'de novo' sites.
source: More than half of the potential target genes (assigned bioinformatically by GREAT) of set 2 'switch' sites overlap with those of set 3 'de novo' sites (60%; Figure 4G, p=5.9e-627), although the latter are much broader.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Pre-engagement by Tcf7l1 may increase the likelihood of additional engagement in neighboring regions of DNA by Lef1 and potentially reinforce transcriptional input into a common gene target.
source: For this overlapping group, pre-engagement by Tcf7l1 may increase the likelihood of additional engagement in neighboring regions of DNA by Lef1 and potentially reinforce transcriptional input into a common gene target.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Results section based on overlap analysis.

claim: Stronger enrichment of active enhancer markers (H3K27ac and RNA Pol II) was observed in low CHIR on set 1 sites predicting indirect Tcf7l1 engagement than set 2 sites where Tcf7l1 was predicted to bind DNA directly.
source: Examining chromatin features and RNA Pol II engagement, we observed stronger enrichment of active enhancer markers (H3K27ac and RNA Pol II) in low CHIR on set 1 sites predicting indirect Tcf7l1 engagement than set 2 sites, where Tcf7l1 was predicted to bind DNA directly through TCF/LEF motifs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Direct binding of TCF7L1/TCF7L2 on set 2 sites was associated with putative enhancers in a less active chromatin state in low CHIR condition.
source: Thus, direct binding of TCF7L1/TCF7L2 on set 2 sites was associated with putative enhancers in a less active chromatin state in low CHIR condition.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on chromatin feature analysis.

claim: A direct analysis of the expression of target gene set of set 2 sites showed the highest expression in high CHIR conditions.
source: Consistent with this view, a direct analysis of the expression of target gene set of set 2 sites showed the highest expression in high CHIR conditions (Figure 4F), suggesting them tending to function in high CHIR.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by expression analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: A dramatic elevation of ATAC-Seq, H3K27ac ChIP-Seq, and RNA Pol II loading signals was observed on β-catenin bound sites in high CHIR condition.
source: A dramatic elevation of all these signals in high CHIR condition (Figure 4H) is consistent with β-catenin engagement enhancing an open chromatin, active enhancer signature.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: High CHIR increased β-catenin association, correlating with switching of TCF/LEF factors at existing active chromatin, de novo opening of new chromatin sites, and an active transcription program initiating nephron formation.
source: Together, the data support the conclusion that high CHIR increased β-catenin association, correlating with switching of TCF/LEF factors at existing active chromatin, de novo opening of new chromatin sites, and an active transcription program initiating nephron formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the collective ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claim: HiCCUPS analysis replicated 19,494 low CHIR and 20,729 high CHIR chromatin–chromatin interaction loops.
source: Analysis of two Hi-C data sets, using HiCCUPS within Juicer Tools (Durand et al., 2016), replicated 19,494 low CHIR and 20,729 high CHIR chromatin–chromatin interaction loops (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Almost half of all loops (40% low CHIR; 44% high CHIR), including those anchored on TSSs (35% low CHIR; 49% high CHIR), were unique to each culture condition.
source: Almost half of all loops (40% low CHIR; 44% high CHIR), including those anchored on TSSs (35% low CHIR; 49% high CHIR), were unique to each culture condition (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Of the 5530 β-catenin-associated sites in high CHIR condition, 28% (1573) were located in loop anchors.
source: Of the 5530 β-catenin-associated sites in high CHIR condition, 28% (1573) were located in loop anchors; 41% (647) of these connected to a TSS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Hi-C and ChIP-seq data integration.

claim: 41% (647) of β-catenin-associated loop anchors connected to a TSS.
source: Of the 5530 β-catenin-associated sites in high CHIR condition, 28% (1573) were located in loop anchors; 41% (647) of these connected to a TSS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Hi-C and ChIP-seq data integration.

claim: Of the 647 β-catenin peaks looped to TSSs, 57% (371) were connected by 'conserved' loops, shared between low CHIR and high CHIR conditions.
source: Of the 647 peaks looped to TSSs, 57% (371) were connected by 'conserved' loops, shared between low CHIR and high CHIR conditions, the remainder appeared de novo under high CHIR conditions (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Among promoters connected to β-catenin-bound enhancers by conserved loops, 56 genes were highly expressed in the high CHIR condition (TPM >5).
source: Among those connected by conserved loops present in both CHIR conditions, 56 genes were highly expressed in the high CHIR condition (TPM >5; Supplementary file 5), including Wnt4, Lhx1, Emx2, Bmp7, and Cxcr4, which associate with NPC differentiation in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Hi-C and RNA-seq data integration.

claim: Genes highly expressed in high CHIR connected by conserved loops include Wnt4, Lhx1, Emx2, Bmp7, and Cxcr4, which associate with NPC differentiation in vivo.
source: Among those connected by conserved loops present in both CHIR conditions, 56 genes were highly expressed in the high CHIR condition (TPM >5; Supplementary file 5), including Wnt4, Lhx1, Emx2, Bmp7, and Cxcr4, which associate with NPC differentiation in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Hi-C and RNA-seq data integration.

claim: In low CHIR conditions, Six2, Tcf7l1, Tcf7l2, and β-catenin bind to the Wnt4 distal enhancer (Wnt4DE).
source: In low CHIR conditions, Six2, Tcf7l1, Tcf7l2, and β-catenin bind to the Wnt4 distal enhancer (Wnt4DE) while in high CHIR, Tcf7 and Lef1 replace Tcf7 and Tcf7l2, with a concomitant decrease in Six2 and increase in β-catenin association (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In high CHIR, Tcf7 and Lef1 replace Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 at the Wnt4DE, with a concomitant decrease in Six2 and increase in β-catenin association.
source: In low CHIR conditions, Six2, Tcf7l1, Tcf7l2, and β-catenin bind to the Wnt4 distal enhancer (Wnt4DE) while in high CHIR, Tcf7 and Lef1 replace Tcf7 and Tcf7l2, with a concomitant decrease in Six2 and increase in β-catenin association (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Two additional loops further upstream of Wnt4 anchor to Ctcf binding sites and loop to the Wnt4 TSS.
source: Two additional loops further upstream anchor to Ctcf binding sites and loop to the Wnt4 TSS (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: All three loops at the Wnt4 locus are stable between low and high CHIR conditions.
source: Interestingly, all three loops are stable between low and high CHIR conditions consistent with a predetermined chromatin organization facilitating rapid activation of a nephron-forming inductive program, on switching the TCF/LEF transcriptional input (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Stable loops at the Wnt4 locus are consistent with a predetermined chromatin organization facilitating rapid activation of a nephron-forming inductive program.
source: Interestingly, all three loops are stable between low and high CHIR conditions consistent with a predetermined chromatin organization facilitating rapid activation of a nephron-forming inductive program, on switching the TCF/LEF transcriptional input (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of Hi-C data.

claim: Lef1 was among the gene sets defined by highly enriched expression in high CHIR conditions with de novo loop formation in high CHIR.
source: Lef1 was among the gene sets defined by highly enriched expression in high CHIR conditions with de novo loop formation in high CHIR (Figure 5E and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The Lef1 locus showed no loop connections to the Lef1 TSS in low CHIR.
source: The Lef1 locus showed no loop connections to the Lef1 TSS in low CHIR.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on Hi-C data.

claim: No TCF/LEF/β-catenin binding was detected around the Lef1 locus in low CHIR, and ATAC-seq and H3K27 acetylation showed only background levels.
source: Further, no TCF/LEF/β-catenin binding was detected, and ATAC-seq and H3K27 acetylation showed only background levels around the Lef1 locus.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claim: Four interaction loops appeared at the Lef1 locus in high CHIR conditions, one of which was associated with a strong Lef1/β-catenin interaction site.
source: In contrast, four interaction loops appeared in high CHIR conditions, one of which was associated with a strong Lef1/β-catenin interaction site, two mapped to CTCF bound regions (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Hi-C and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In high CHIR, a string of LEF1/TCF7/β-catenin binding events accompanied enhanced accessibility (ATAC-seq) and the appearance of an active chromatin signature (H3K27ac) at the Lef1 locus.
source: In high CHIR, a string of LEF1/TCF7/β-catenin binding events accompanied enhanced accessibility (ATAC-seq) and the appearance of an active chromatin signature (H3K27ac) (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: De novo loop formation at the Lef1 locus may follow from de novo interaction of LEF1/TCF7/β-catenin binding complexes at the Lef1 enhancer, in a feedback mechanism driving NPC commitment.
source: These data suggest that de novo loop formation may follow from de novo interaction of LEF1/TCF7/β-catenin binding complexes at the Lef1 enhancer, in a feedback mechanism driving NPC commitment (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of Hi-C and ChIP-seq data.

claim: In low CHIR, NPC maintenance and expansion conditions, the mitogenic activity mediated through CHIR stimulation of Wnt signaling appears to be independent of TCF/LEF binding to TCF/LEF motifs in target genes.
source: (1) In low CHIR, NPC maintenance and expansion conditions, the mitogenic activity mediated through CHIR stimulation of Wnt signaling appears to be independent of TCF/LEF binding to TCF/LEF motifs in target genes.
evidence: This is a key conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: CHIR-mediated elevation of β-catenin is accompanied by reduced expression of mRNAs for transcriptional inhibitory TCF factors (Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2) and dramatic increase in expression of mRNAs for activating forms (Tcf7 and Lef1), promoting an inductive program.
source: (2) CHIR-mediated elevation of β-catenin is accompanied by reduced expression of mRNAs for transcriptional inhibitory TCF factors (Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2) and dramatic increase in expression of mRNAs for activating forms (Tcf7 and Lef1), promoting an inductive program.
evidence: This is a key conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Direct binding of inhibitory Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 engagement at target motifs within putative cis-regulatory elements prefigures engagement of Tcf7 and Lef1 in a chromatin landscape primed for the transcriptional activation of the nephron-forming program.
source: (3) Direct binding of inhibitory Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 engagement at target motifs within putative cis-regulatory elements prefigures engagement of Tcf7 and Lef1 in a chromatin landscape primed for the transcriptional activation of the nephron-forming program.
evidence: This is a key conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: High CHIR invokes a switch from inhibitory to activating TCF/LEF engagement at enhancers promoting nephron differentiation consistent with β-catenin controlling TCF/LEF target engagement.
source: (4) High CHIR invokes a switch from inhibitory to activating TCF/LEF engagement at enhancers promoting nephron differentiation consistent with β-catenin controlling TCF/LEF target engagement.
evidence: This is a key conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: In addition to enhancer–promoter loops pre-established in uncommitted NPCs, TCF/LEF/β-catenin interactions at de novo sites may play additional roles in the inductive process, including positive feedback in the Lef1 program promoting nephrogenesis.
source: (5) In addition to enhancer–promoter loops pre-established in uncommitted NPCs associated with switching of inhibitory to activating TCF/LEF binding signatures on high CHIR induction, TCF/LEF/ β-catenin interactions at de novo sites may play additional roles in the inductive process, including positive feedback in the Lef1 program promoting nephrogenesis.
evidence: This is a key conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Among the 85 genes associated with the term 'cell cycle', only one gene showed significant β-catenin association within 500 kb of the TSS in low CHIR.
source: However, among the 85 genes associated with the term 'cell cycle,' only one gene showed significant β-catenin association within 500 kb of the TSS in low CHIR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), arguing against a scenario that directs transcriptional regulation of these genes through β-catenin engagement.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: β-catenin may act through an alternative transcriptional mechanism in NPC maintenance.
source: These findings raise the possibility that β-catenin acts through an alternative transcriptional mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section based on the lack of direct TCF/LEF binding at cell cycle genes.

claim: β-catenin may play an essential, non-transcriptional role that links to control of cell proliferation.
source: Alternatively, β-catenin may play an essential, non-transcriptional role that links to control of cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: TCF-β-catenin nuclear complexes have been reported to oscillate with the cell cycle, suggesting potential nuclear roles independent of DNA association.
source: TCF-β-catenin nuclear complexes have been reported to oscillate with the cell cycle, suggesting potential nuclear roles independent of DNA association (Ding et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: β-catenin is reported to play an essential, non-transcriptional role in self-renewal of mouse epiblast stem cells.
source: Further, β-catenin is reported to play an essential, non-transcriptional role in self-renewal of mouse epiblast stem cells (Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: CHIR-mediated inhibition of GSK3 outside of β-catenin regulation might play a role in NPC maintenance.
source: Additionally, CHIR-mediated inhibition of GSK3 outside of β-catenin regulation might play a role.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: GSK3 inhibition by Wnt ligand administration leads to deubiquitylation and stabilization of target proteins.
source: Interestingly, Acebron et al., 2014 have reported that GSK3 inhibition by Wnt ligand administration leads to deubiquitylation and stabilization of target proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In mouse embryonic stem cell (ESC) culture, canonical Wnt signaling, induced by CHIR, supports long-term self-renewal of ESCs.
source: In mouse embryonic stem cell (ESC) culture, canonical Wnt signaling, induced by CHIR, supports long-term self-renewal of ESCs (Ying et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In mouse ESCs, Tcf7l1 has been shown to repress expression of genes involved in stem cell maintenance while Tcf7 and Lef1 activate targets.
source: Tcf7l1 has been shown to repress expression of genes involved in stem cell maintenance while Tcf7 and Lef1 activate targets (Yi et al., 2011; Wray et al., 2011) consistent with a classic canonical Wnt transcriptional activation program of stem cell renewal.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In mouse ESCs, β-catenin may block the negative interplay of Tcf7l1 binding at the Sox motif of Sox-Oct bound stem cell promoting enhancers.
source: However, other studies directly analyzing β-catenin interactions at the chromatin level suggest an indirect process where β-catenin may block the negative interplay of Tcf7l1 binding at the Sox motif of Sox-Oct bound stem cell promoting enhancers (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In the ESC system, β-catenin target sites containing TCF/LEF motif correlate strongly with differentiation promoting targets.
source: In this ESC system, β-catenin target sites containing TCF/LEF motif correlate strongly with differentiation promoting targets, consistent with the normal role of β-catenin in vivo in regulating gastrulation (Haegel et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: Depletion of both Tcf7l1 and Tcf7 is sufficient to maintain Wnt ligand-independent expansion of ESCs.
source: Further, depletion of both Tcf7l1 and Tcf7 is sufficient to maintain Wnt ligand-independent expansion of ESCs, consistent with the implication that β-catenin activation can abrogate the repressive effect of Tcf7l11 independent of an activator Tcf7 (Yi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In hair follicle stem cells (HFSC), Wnt induces a transition of the stem cells from the quiescent to the proliferative state.
source: In hair follicle stem cells (HFSC), Wnt induces a transition of the stem cells from the quiescent to the proliferative state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 are preferentially expressed in HFSC, while Lef1 and Tcf7 are preferentially expressed in the differentiated HFSC, that is, hair germ cells.
source: Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 are preferentially expressed in HFSC, while Lef1 and Tcf7 are preferentially expressed in the differentiated HFSC, that is, hair germ cells (Merrill et al., 2001; Lien et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In HFSCs, TCF7L1/TCF7L2 repress genes involved in HFSC differentiation, which are activated by Tcf7/Lef1, correlating with replacement of TCF7L1/TCF7L2 by Tcf7/Lef1 on relevant enhancers.
source: TCF7L1/TCF7L2 repress genes involved in HFSC differentiation, which are activated by Tcf7/Lef1, correlating with replacement of TCF7L1/TCF7L2 by Tcf7/Lef1 on relevant enhancers, a close parallel to activity in NPC programs described here (Adam et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: In the Wnt-off state, Tcf factors recruit Groucho family co-repressors and histone deacetylase to repress Wnt target gene expression.
source: In the Wnt-off state, Tcf factors are known to recruit Groucho family co-repressors (Cavallo et al., 1998) and histone deacetylase (Billin et al., 2000) to repress Wnt target gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: Upon Wnt ligand stimulation, Groucho is replaced by β-catenin for activation.
source: Upon Wnt ligand stimulation, Groucho is replaced by β-catenin for activation (Brantjes et al., 2001; Daniels and Weis, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: β-catenin has been shown to be able to recruit various chromatin modulators, including histone acetyl transferase, histone methyl transferase, and chromatin remodeler.
source: From evidence in vitro, β-catenin has been shown to be able to recruit various chromatin modulators, including histone acetyl transferase (Hecht et al., 2000), histone methyl transferase (Sierra et al., 2006), and chromatin remodeler (Barker et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: Through interaction with Pygo and Bcl9, as well as direct interaction, β-catenin can form a complex with the Mediator complex, which bridges the Tcf-bound enhancer to RNA Pol II complex at the target gene promoter.
source: Furthermore, through interaction with Pygo and Bcl9 (Kramps et al., 2002; Schwab et al., 2007), as well as direct interaction (Kim et al., 2006), β-catenin can form a complex with the Mediator complex, which bridges the Tcf-bound enhancer to RNA Pol II complex at the target gene promoter (Jeronimo and Robert, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: Six2 binding at certain TCF/LEF targets in NPCs might confer a repressive effect; Six2 interacts with histone deacetylation complexes (HDACs), and depletion of the HDACs in NPC elevates Wnt4 and Lef1 expression.
source: In addition, Six2 binding at certain TCF/LEF targets in NPCs might also confer a repressive effect; Six2 interacts with histone deacetylation complexes (HDACs), and depletion of the HDACs in NPC elevates Wnt4 and Lef1 expression (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: The repressive chromatin modifiers Ezh1 and Ezh2 repress Wnt4 and Lef1 expression in NPC through maintaining H3K27me3 mark.
source: Similarly, the repressive chromatin modifiers Ezh1 and Ezh2 also repress Wnt4 and Lef1 expression in NPC through maintaining H3K27me3 mark (Liu et al., 2020), although the repressive functions of such chromatin modifiers tend to have broader effects.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: During development certain enhancer–promoter loops are stable in Drosophila, that is, the enhancer–promoter loop is established before the target gene is activated as a mechanism to prime developmentally potent cells to differentiate into predestined cell fates.
source: Studies in Drosophila have indicated that during development certain enhancer–promoter loops are stable (Ghavi-Helm et al., 2014), that is, the enhancer–promoter loop is established before the target gene is activated as a mechanism to prime developmentally potent cells to differentiate into predestined cell fates.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation support.

claim: Analysis of Hi-C data shows that enhancer–promoter loops present in low CHIR condition are consistent with NPCs exhibiting a primed genomic state promoting nephron-forming programs.
source: Analysis of Hi-C data shows that enhancer–promoter loops present in low CHIR condition are consistent with NPCs exhibiting a primed genomic state promoting nephron-forming programs.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on Hi-C data.

claim: Approximately 56% of loops observed in high CHIR were observed in low CHIR.
source: Approximately 56% of loops observed in high CHIR were observed in low CHIR.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on Hi-C data.

claim: Of conserved loops, 70% connected to a TSS.
source: Of these, 70% connected to a TSS (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Hi-C data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 engagement at enhancer–promoter regions may maintain the primed state during an extensive period of progenitor expansion in the course of kidney development.
source: These findings also raise an interesting possibility that Tcf7l1 and Tcf7l2 engagement at such enhancer–promoter regions may maintain the primed state during an extensive period of progenitor expansion in the course of kidney development.
